findings.title: Promise, delay, and the false claim that briefly works
findings.claim: At the focus, al-Haqq and al-batil acquire a time-and-performance test: the haqq-like claim endures as its promise is fulfilled, whereas an alternative may be attractive or briefly useful yet fail to complete what it seems to promise.
findings.mechanism: The focus al-Haqq is carried by the binding-necessity branch and al-batil by the loss-of-lasting-validity branch. Beyond the pericope, 31:9 and 31:33 pair a promise with haqq, while 31:24 inserts brief enjoyment and 31:33 names deceptive allure. Their contact makes fulfillment across delay, rather than simple existence versus nonexistence, a further way to read the contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice how a false claim may offer real short-term benefit or attraction and still fail as a lasting commitment.
findings.containment: This adds a promise-performance reading without reducing al-Haqq to a title defined only by promises. The local confirmation of each promise remains live, and al-batil is not presented as experiential nothingness.

findings.title: Divine rank beside human self-display
findings.claim: The focus's paired highness and greatness predicates retain their height, magnitude, rank, and mastery range while also reading as warranted divine rank beside the human attempt to enlarge oneself; the cross-run inference grounds that contrast in consequence-bearing governance.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers al-Ali and al-Kabir meet 31:18's ban on proud display, swagger, and boasting. The wider human trigger returns through both predicates, shifting the reading from an unqualified superlative to a contrast between effective divine rank and performed human inflation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that the focus's titles need not describe self-display merely on a larger scale; they also mark a different grounding for rank.
findings.containment: This adds rather than replaces the spatial, quantitative, noble-rank, and mastery senses. The governance explanation is a trusted cross-run interpretation, while the exact external trigger supplies a pride contrast rather than a full account of divine action.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch records and cross-run support are trusted/registered, but the 31:18 context word-level trigger and the governance inference also rely on legacy-unbound HFT evidence.
